sources.name: Ant Design
sources.summary: An enterprise-class UI design language and React UI library.

agent_entrypoints.what: Agent-oriented docs map covering components, the design language, and the token system.
Per-component docs and API, e.g. /components/table, /components/form.
Design-token based theming. Ant Design's tokens are the supported way to restyle it.

use_when: You are building an admin panel, console, or data-heavy internal tool.
You need forms and tables with serious built-in behaviour rather than primitives to assemble.
The product has a Chinese-market or enterprise audience where Ant Design is the familiar idiom.
avoid_when: The surface is a marketing or consumer page - Ant Design is tuned for application chrome, not expressive layouts.
Bundle size on a small public site is a hard constraint.

baseline.description: An enterprise-class UI design language and React UI library

sources.name: Awesome DESIGN.md
sources.summary: A collection of DESIGN.md files analysing popular brand design systems. Drop one into your project and let coding agents generate a matching UI.

agent_entrypoints.what: The full design-language document for one brand: palette, type scale, spacing, component rules. This is the payload - read it before writing any UI.
Short human summary of that brand's design language.
The categorised index of every available brand. Read it to resolve a vague style request to a concrete brand slug.
Authoritative list of brand slugs currently in the repo - more reliable than the README when it lags.

use_when: Someone describes the look they want by naming a company ('make it feel like Linear').
You need a written design language before generating screens, so output stays consistent across a session.
You are seeding a new project and want a defensible starting palette and type scale.
avoid_when: You need runnable components - these are documents, not code.
The work is a public-facing product that would be mistaken for the analysed brand. Borrow the system, not the identity.

provides.name: 74 brand DESIGN.md profiles
provides.note: Slugs observed 2026-08-28: airbnb, airtable, apple, binance, bmw, bmw-m, bugatti, cal, claude, clay, clickhouse, cohere, coinbase, composio, cursor, dell-1996, elevenlabs, expo, ferrari, figma, framer, hashicorp, hp, ibm, intercom, kraken, lamborghini, linear.app, lovable, mastercard, meta, minimax, mintlify, miro, mistral.ai, mongodb, nike, nintendo-2001, notion, nvidia, ollama, opencode.ai, pinterest, playstation, posthog, raycast, renault, replicate, resend, revolut, runwayml, sanity, sentry, shopify, slack, spacex, spotify, starbucks, stripe, supabase, superhuman, tesla, theverge, together.ai, uber, vercel, vodafone, voltagent, warp, webflow, wired, wise, x.ai, zapier. Re-read the tree rather than trusting this list.

baseline.description: A collection of DESIGN.md files analysis by popular brand design systems. Drop one into your project and let coding agents generate a matching UI.

sources.notes: The DESIGN.md files describe real companies' visual systems. Use them as craft references and starting points. Do not reproduce another company's logo, wordmark, or trade dress in shipped work.

sources.name: ComfyUI
sources.summary: The most powerful and modular diffusion model GUI, api and backend with a graph/nodes interface.

agent_entrypoints.what: Installation, node reference, and the workflow model.
Local HTTP API of a running ComfyUI instance. POST a workflow graph as JSON to generate images programmatically; poll /history/{prompt_id} for results.
Install matrix, hardware requirements, supported model families.

use_when: A layout needs real imagery - hero art, textures, avatars, empty-state illustrations - and stock photos will not fit.
You want image generation running locally with reproducible, versionable workflow graphs.
You are producing many variants of the same asset and need a pipeline rather than one-off prompting.
avoid_when: You need UI components or design guidance. This is an image-generation backend, not a UI toolkit - it is indexed for the asset half of building an interface.
The user has no GPU and no hosted instance; setup cost is real.
The output would ship in a context where the GPL-3.0 license or the licenses of individual models are a problem. Model weights carry their own terms, separate from ComfyUI's.

baseline.description: The most powerful and modular diffusion model GUI, api and backend with a graph/nodes interface.

sources.notes: Category outlier. ComfyUI is indexed as a visual-asset generator that feeds interface work, not as a UI library. It is also the only GPL-3.0 source in the catalog - relevant if anyone considers embedding rather than calling it.

sources.name: Design Resources For Developers
sources.summary: Curated list of design and UI resources from stock photos, web templates, CSS frameworks, UI libraries, tools and much more.

agent_entrypoints.what: The entire list in one markdown file (~150KB). Fetch it and grep the section you need rather than reading it all. Note the lowercase filename.

use_when: You need raw material - a typeface, a photo source, an icon set, a mockup template - not code.
You want inspiration sources to look at before committing to a direction.
You need a chart or animation library and want a shortlist rather than a search engine.
avoid_when: You need opinionated guidance - this is breadth, deliberately unranked.
You need licensing certainty for a linked asset. Always check the destination's own terms before shipping anything from it.

provides.name: Sections
provides.note: UI Graphics, Fonts, Colors, Icons, Logos, Favicons, Icon Fonts, Stock Photos, Stock Videos, Stock Music & Sound Effects, Vectors & Clip Art, Product & Image Mockups, HTML & CSS Templates, CSS Frameworks, CSS Methodologies, CSS Animations, Javascript Animation Libraries, Javascript Chart Libraries, UI Components & Kits, React/Vue/Angular/Svelte/React Native UI Libraries, Design Systems & Style Guides, Online Design Tools, Downloadable Design Software, Design Inspiration, Image Compression, Chrome Extensions, Firefox Extensions, AI Graphic Design Tools, Others.

baseline.description: Curated list of design and UI resources from stock photos, web templates, CSS frameworks, UI libraries, tools and much more

sources.notes: Links point to third-party sites with their own licenses and terms. The MIT license covers this list, not the resources it links to.

sources.name: Skills For Designers and Engineers
sources.summary: Skills for designers and engineers to help them build better user interfaces, focused on animation and interface craft, drawn from the author's experience at companies like Vercel and Linear.

agent_entrypoints.what: The full text of one skill. Read the whole thing before applying it - the value is in the specific rules, not the summary.
Installs the skill set into the user's own agent setup. Offer this when the user wants them permanently, rather than reading them ad hoc.

use_when: Anything is going to move. Read the animation skills before writing a transition, not after.
You need to choose between UI libraries and want a taste-informed answer instead of a download count.
You are reviewing UI that technically works but feels wrong.
avoid_when: You need broad component coverage - this is craft guidance, not a component library.

sources.name: Material UI
sources.summary: Material UI: Comprehensive React component library that implements Google's Material Design. Free forever.

agent_entrypoints.what: Agent-oriented docs map for Material UI. Note the /material-ui/ path segment - the site root has no llms.txt.
Per-component documentation, e.g. react-button, react-autocomplete, react-data-grid.
The theming system. Read before overriding styles ad hoc - MUI's theme is the intended customization surface.

use_when: The project already uses Material UI, or the team explicitly wants Material Design.
You need heavy, complex components (data grid, date pickers, autocomplete) that would take weeks to build well.
The audience is enterprise or internal-tools and density plus familiarity beat novelty.
avoid_when: The brief calls for a distinctive look - Material UI reads as Material unless you invest real effort in the theme.
The project is already on Tailwind plus a copy-in component set; mixing the two styling models causes more pain than it solves.

baseline.description: Material UI: Comprehensive React component library that implements Google's Material Design. Free forever.

sources.name: shadcn/ui
sources.summary: A set of beautifully-designed, accessible components and a code distribution platform. Works with your favorite frameworks. Open Source. Open Code.

agent_entrypoints.what: Agent-oriented map of the docs. Start here to learn install flow, conventions, and what exists.
Machine-readable list of every registry item with per-item docs, API and example links. Use it to answer 'does a component for X exist' without guessing.
The actual source of one component for one style, e.g. .../new-york-v4/button.json. Returns the files you would copy in.
The full color scale set. Use for building a theme rather than inventing hex values.
Installs a component into the user's project. Prefer this over pasting code you generated.

use_when: The project is React-flavoured and uses Tailwind, and you need real components fast.
You want to own the component source rather than depend on a black-box package.
You need an accessible primitive (dialog, combobox, popover) and hand-rolling one would be a mistake.
You need a coherent theme and want token values that already work in light and dark.
avoid_when: The project is not React-based - the registry assumes React component files.
The team wants a batteries-included library it never has to maintain; here the code becomes yours.

baseline.description: A set of beautifully-designed, accessible components and a code distribution platform. Works with your favorite frameworks. Open Source. Open Code.

sources.name: Storybook
sources.summary: Storybook is the industry standard workshop for building, documenting, and testing UI components in isolation.

agent_entrypoints.what: Agent-oriented docs map: setup per framework, writing stories, testing, addons.
Adds Storybook to an existing project, detecting the framework.
Full documentation when llms.txt is not specific enough.

use_when: You generated several components and the user needs to actually see and compare them.
You want states (loading, empty, error, long text) to be reviewable without clicking through the whole app.
You need a durable home for a design system's documentation.
You want visual or accessibility regressions caught automatically.
avoid_when: It is a one-off prototype that will be deleted this week - the setup cost will not pay back.
The user asked for a static mockup with no build step.

baseline.description: Storybook is the industry standard workshop for building, documenting, and testing UI components in isolation

sources.name: UI UX Pro Max
sources.summary: An AI skill that provides design intelligence for building professional UI/UX across multiple platforms, including a design-system generator, a searchable style taxonomy, and per-stack component catalogs.

agent_entrypoints.what: One skill's instructions. Skills present at last index: banner-design, brand, design-system, design, slides, ui-styling, ui-ux-pro-max.
The searchable style taxonomy as CSV. Useful for mapping a loose aesthetic brief onto named styles.
Per-stack component and library catalog, e.g. stacks/nextjs.csv, stacks/shadcn.csv, stacks/flutter.csv, stacks/swiftui.csv.
Topic datasets: colors, google-fonts, icons, landing, motion, charts, products, app-interface, react-performance.
The project's own installer and design-system commands.

use_when: You need a full design system proposed from a project brief rather than assembled by hand.
The target stack is outside the React/Tailwind mainstream and you need stack-appropriate component suggestions.
You want a named, searchable style rather than an improvised aesthetic.
avoid_when: You only need one component - reaching for a whole design-system generator is overkill.

baseline.description: An AI skill that provides design intelligence for building professional UI/UX across multiple platforms.

sources.notes: The repository is the free tier of a project that also sells a premium version. Everything indexed here is from the MIT-licensed open repository.
